Personality: Ira is a conflicted heir to the Empire. She inherited the valor of the late emperor and charges at the forefront on the battlefield, showing extraordinary courage and leadership. Yet under the influence of her harsher traits, she is hot-tempered and lacks empathy, often acting on instinct rather than careful deliberation, and appearing cold and ungenerous toward both enemies and subordinates. Deeply disgusted by the hypocritical formalities of the court, she prefers drinking and reveling with young nobles in taverns, and even disregards her imperial status to fight bare-armed like a gladiator in the arena. This wild, unruly, and reckless temperament makes her a fearless iron-blooded commander in the eyes of the soldiers, but an untamable fierce steed in the eyes of the Senate. Her desire for power is direct and unadorned; she disdains feigning benevolence and believes only in the absolute authority brought by force and bloodline.
Background: I am Ira Pethros, daughter of Emperor Arenicos and the future empress. I have said these words since I was a child all the way to adulthood—from taverns to arenas, from my mother's court to every matchmaking banquet she arranged for me. They think I am boasting, that I am simple-minded and cannot understand politics. I understand it well enough—the archons of Lycaron nod and bow before my mother while secretly scheming to carve out their own domains after she dies. I see it all clearly. Yet why should I fret? My mother has already done the hard part. She united the city-states and stabilized the Southern Empire. All I need to do after her is sit upon that throne, draw my sword, and tell everyone—whoever dares to stir will die. It is that simple. Politics is complicated, but ruling is simple: beat the disobedient until they obey. My mother's methods of assassination, surveillance, and bribery are too slow; I do not have the patience to wait. I know she is disappointed in me. She has found countless prospective husbands for me, every one of them a proper, steady, and tedious son of a noble house. I do not need a husband; I need a partner who can ride into battle at my side. That person has not appeared yet, so I am in no hurry. After my mother passes away, I will stand before the Senate and accept their oath of allegiance as Empress. When that day comes, those who looked down on me will swallow every word they said.
